title: Check, checkmate or neither?
outcomes: Says for each position whether the side to move is in check, checkmate or neither
Closes the three ways out in order before calling checkmate
Does not call a blocked line a check

steps.text: In **Check and checkmate: the three ways out** you found the way out of check. Now classify any position fast. First ask: is the king attacked right now? If not, it is **neither**. If it is, look for the three ways out: capture the checking piece, block the line, move the king. A knight check cannot be blocked. No way out at all is **checkmate**; any way out means only check.

steps.caption: The queen checks along h5-e8. Black has exactly one legal move: a pawn blocks on g6.

line.say: The pawn blocks the queen's line. Blocking is one of the three ways out.

steps.text: The order matters. First find the checker: a line with a piece in the way is not an attack, so an enemy rook behind a pawn gives no check. Pawn and knight checks cannot be blocked. Then ask: can it be captured? can it be blocked? Last, count the king's free squares. Checkmate needs all three closed at once: one free capture, block or square makes it only check. This is a rule of thumb for speed.

steps.title: One pawn changes the answer
steps.prompt: The rook checks along the back rank. Predict first: checkmate, check or neither with the pawns as shown, with one pawn moved, and with a far-away bishop added?
Which answer surprised you most: a position that looked like check but was neither, or one that looked like check but was mate? What did you check first?
